chapter: Joe Lyde stories and bandstand tales
title: Bandstand mishaps: dozing players, the Saints and Ice's real bass
summary: Anecdotes about Archie Rogers dozing, a trumpeter asleep in Alabama, Zanco's pinched finger on the Saints, and Bob Ice playing a real bass in Europe.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, I tell you, I've seen, uh, I've seen Archie Rogers in between numbers almost go to sleep on the bandstand. He'll, to me, he actually looks like he dozes. And on the next tune, he's as live as can be.
When you guys did that? They saved their lip, that wifey. Now having a long job. You fall asleep during the numbers.
Roll up that old King B, ready for the next tune.

I hear a trumpet player that I worked, right up around Tuscaloosa, Alabama, one night in Birmingham. He got pretty loaded and, uh, he went to sleep while we were playing, uh, uh, loud up-tempo number. So they let him sleep and they woke him up in the middle of the next number, which was, uh, one, if you pardon the expression, a belly-rubbing number. So he jumped up and he started playing this real hot, loud bass number right in the middle of the slow one. They told him to shut up and he sat back down and went to sleep and they woke him up again to take us over and, no, they woke him up again at intermission. He thought the job was over, so he packed up and left.

You know, well, speaking of Alabama, getting back to Alabama, uh, Briss brought my attention to it the other night. I really had forgotten about it. But, uh, we were playing when the Saints go marching in. When we were playing his debutant deal. And, uh, to me, I mean, the Saints is more of a, you know, it's just the same thing. You're playing the same thing over and over and over and over again, say, until the tune is finished. But, uh, that particular night, my finger got caught between two of the valves on my horn. And, uh, honestly, that's the best and the hardest I've ever played on the Saints. I don't know, I don't know, I could never do it again, see. But actually, that's what happened. My finger got between the first and second valve. And that's the best the Saints ever came off for me.
Jeff told me about the time he got his neck tied stuck between the...
Yeah, he got his tie caught in the strings of his banjo, you know. And, boy.
Now, one of the musicians wear bow ties.
Something happened to Ice, too, didn't it? One night?

Oh, uh, when we were, we were playing over in Europe, Ice broke a string on his bass. He plays his two-string bass. And he broke a string on his, on his bass. And the only thing that could be had was a regular bass, a real bass. They put it in his hands and he played it. He played just as good as he'd ever played. He played a regular... Of course, he only used the two strings, but I mean, he looked important standing up there with a real bass in his hands, you know.
Well, I know what he did, but I ain't gonna tell it.
I remember. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. I remember.
